items.summary: The Houthis said they carried out a new wave of attacks targeting two civilian airports — Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport and Najran Airport near the southern Saudi-Yemen border — plus the Royal Saudi Air Force's King Khalid Air Base, using cruise and ballistic missiles. Saudi authorities said three Saudi nationals were killed and several people of various nationalities injured across two attacks on the airport Thursday; falling missile debris damaged a kindergarten and a medical clinic. Houthi leader warned Saudi Arabia to prepare for a long conflict.
items.title: Oct 8: Houthi missile wave hits Riyadh airport, Najran airport and Saudi air base; 3 Saudis killed

items.summary: A Houthi missile struck Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, killing 13 people — four Saudis, two Bangladeshis, an American, an Egyptian, a Jordanian, a Syrian, a Palestinian, a Sudanese, and later an Indian citizen who died of wounds — and wounding 309+. Security footage showed the terminal ceiling collapsing as passengers fled. Saudi Arabia's deadliest attack in more than a decade; the Saudi-led coalition called it a war crime.
items.title: Oct 10: Deadly Houthi missile strike on Riyadh's King Khalid airport kills 13, wounds 300+

items.summary: Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed responsibility for the Oct 10 airport strike in a televised speech. The same day, an unidentified projectile hit Terminal 4 at King Khalid airport, killing one Pakistani resident, wounding 11 and starting a fire; Saudi air defenses intercepted a cruise missile nearby. Dammam's King Fahd International Airport also came under attack, and the Houthis claimed strikes on two Saudi Aramco facilities. Riyadh schools shifted to remote learning Sun–Thu; the US Mission issued security alerts for US citizens.
items.title: Oct 11: Houthis claim Riyadh strike; Terminal 4 hit (1 killed, 11 wounded), Dammam airport and Aramco sites targeted

items.summary: A fresh Houthi drone and cruise-missile wave targeted the kingdom's key oil and gas facilities; several were intercepted. King Khalid airport stays closed until at least Oct 17 (NOTAM) with 46% of flights cancelled across Saudi airports; the FAA warned US airlines on Saudi routes. The World Petroleum Congress in Riyadh was disrupted — the CEOs of ExxonMobil, TotalEnergies, Shell and BP withdrew. Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdul Aziz bin Salman vowed a serious retaliation.
items.title: Oct 12: Fresh Houthi wave targets Saudi oil/gas sites; Riyadh airport shut till Oct 17, energy summit disrupted

items.summary: Turkey, Pakistan, Egypt and Saudi Arabia (the 'R4') jointly condemned the Houthi airport attacks as a 'dangerous escalation', backing all legitimate Saudi countermeasures and holding the Houthi militia fully accountable. The four signed a joint defence pact in August under which an attack on one is an attack on all; Turkey is assessing defensive/technical support for Riyadh but ruled out troop deployment and offensive operations.
items.title: Oct 12: Turkey, Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia jointly condemn attacks under defence pact
Trump weighs US military intervention after Riyadh airport strikes
items.summary: President Trump said he is evaluating whether the US should join Saudi strikes against the Tehran-backed Houthis in Yemen — "We may. We're going to look at it. We just found out about the recent attack. So we'll make a decision. We move very quickly." He also plans to speak with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. Secretary of State Marco Rubio condemned the attacks and reaffirmed US support for the kingdom. Context: the US had agreed a ceasefire with the Houthis after a month-long bombing campaign, and neither side appeared eager to resume fighting.

items.title: Houthis claim 119 Saudi attacks in 24 hours killed 11+ civilians, threaten more airport strikes
items.summary: The Houthis said Saudi warplanes and missile units carried out 119 attacks over the past 24 hours, claiming at least 11 civilians including women and children were killed — a claim CNN notes it cannot independently verify. The group said the airport strikes were a response to the intensified Saudi air campaign in Yemen and threatened to continue targeting airports and other sites inside the kingdom.

items.title: Riyadh airport shut 'until further notice'; Lufthansa, Air France-KLM, Etihad extend suspensions
items.summary: King Khalid International Airport will remain closed until further notice (NOTAM: at least Oct 17) to verify safety of facilities. Cirium data: 99.7% of Sunday's scheduled flights cancelled, ~60% of Monday's expected cancelled; FlightRadar24 put Riyadh cancellations near 78%. Lufthansa cancelled all Riyadh flights until Oct 16, Air France-KLM extended its suspension to the end of the month, and Etihad extended cancellations (~20 flights to Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam). EASA widened its Saudi airspace warning; the FAA caution stands. New Al Arabiya security footage shows Saturday's terminal blast collapsing part of the ceiling as passengers fled.

items.title: UK tells citizens to avoid Jeddah, Dammam and Saudi airports; Thursday jet attack killed pilot
items.summary: The UK Foreign Office advised British citizens to avoid travel to Jeddah and Dammam and to all Saudi airports except Medina's. A Thursday advisory already covered Riyadh after a Houthi attack on a passenger jet killed the pilot and two others — Saudia confirmed one of its jets was damaged with no passengers aboard. The advisories land as Riyadh prepares to host the Future Investment Initiative ('Davos in the Desert') later this month.

items.title: Mecca defence pact activated: Pakistan/Turkey pledged rapid deployment; Houthis hold Bab al-Mandeb
items.summary: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan activated the Mecca mutual defence pact on Oct 5 ('collective deterrence'), pledging rapid deployment of forces to the kingdom. Pakistan — with ~8,000 troops, JF-17 fighters and HQ-9 air defences already in-country — and Turkey committed to reconnaissance/support roles while Saudi forces lead combat; Turkey's FM ruled out Turkish troop deployment or offensive operations pending parliamentary ratification. Backdrop: a Saudi-backed Yemeni counteroffensive with ~100 coalition jets aims to retake the Bab al-Mandeb strait seized by the Houthis in September, while the rebels tighten their siege of Taiz.

items.title: Saudi Arabia asked Trump for urgent support; he declined, US says
items.summary: Saudi Arabia requested urgent support from President Trump after the weekend airport strikes, but he declined as US forces remain tied up in the simmering conflict with Iran, The Times reports. The nuance matters: Trump is still publicly weighing joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis. Separately, the Houthi coastal offensive has driven up oil prices, and the campaign is believed to have been coordinated with Iran, strengthening Tehran's leverage as it moves to blockade the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: No confirmed fresh airport strike Monday; GACA gives no reopening date
items.summary: Aviation tracker AirMedia24 found no GACA statement or wire report of a fresh strike on Riyadh airport Monday — viral posts about a new drone attack are unverified, likely recycled footage of Saturday's blast and Sunday's Terminal 4 strike; the most recent confirmed airport deaths remain Oct 11. GACA extended the suspension Monday with no reopening date announced (the Oct 17 NOTAM is provisional and unconfirmed by GACA). Dammam and Abha saw disruption; Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Doha and Jeddah remain open with knock-on delays. The damaged terminals sit inside the $7.2B King Salman International Airport expansion site.

items.title: Saudi defences intercept drone over Eastern Province, ballistic missile toward Khamis Mushait
items.summary: Saudi-led coalition forces said air defences intercepted and destroyed a drone in the Eastern Province and a ballistic missile launched toward Khamis Mushait; emergency alerts were issued in Abha early Monday but the danger has since passed, Saudi Civil Defence said. Meanwhile a Saudi ministry says conferences in Riyadh — including the upcoming Future Investment Initiative — are going ahead despite the attacks.

items.title: Saudi Arabia running low on Patriot interceptors, WSJ reports
items.summary: Saudi officials told the Wall Street Journal the kingdom's stock of Patriot interceptors is running short after two consecutive days of Houthi missile fire on Riyadh airport. The Journal also reports the US has so far resisted Saudi requests for direct help reversing Houthi territorial gains in Yemen — though on Oct 2 Washington deployed two additional Patriot batteries to the Gulf, one to Saudi Arabia to protect a major oil facility and one to Qatar for a gas installation.

items.title: Saudi-led coalition hits Houthi Red Sea coast positions; Sanaa airstrikes reported
items.summary: The Saudi-led coalition says it struck Houthi military positions along Yemen's Red Sea coast, including weapons depots and facilities allegedly used to store explosive boats and naval mines, and says it thwarted a planned Houthi maritime attack. Airstrikes on Sanaa were also reported. Claims about targets destroyed and fighters killed are not independently verified — this is the first reported retaliation since the energy minister's vow.

items.title: Saudi Arabia says it intercepted a ballistic missile headed for Riyadh on Monday
items.summary: Saudi Arabia said it intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched toward Riyadh on Monday, as King Khalid airport stayed shut. The past week's Houthi attacks have killed at least 20 people and wounded hundreds, per CNN's tally. Hours earlier, civil aviation said the airport stays closed until further notice (NOTAM: at least Oct 17) pending safety verification.

items.title: Coalition claims 136 Houthi targets destroyed; Sanaa airport hit Sunday
items.summary: The Saudi-led coalition says large-scale airstrikes destroyed 136 Houthi military targets — missile storage, command centers and depots — to degrade their ballistic-missile capability; Houthi-run Al-Masirah confirmed strikes in Saada province. Saudi forces also struck Sanaa International Airport on Sunday (no casualty reports yet, per Saba). The Houthis counter-claim 124 Saudi airstrikes over the weekend and say 91 people, mostly women and children, have been killed since Sept 3 (unverified); the UN puts the latest fighting's toll near 1,000 killed and 200,000+ displaced.

items.title: MBS reportedly pushing Trump to take military action against Houthis
items.summary: Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has reportedly been pressing President Trump to take military action against the Houthis, who agreed to a ceasefire with the US last year. Trump said Saturday the US may join Saudi strikes — a reversal after Washington repeatedly declined Riyadh's requests. The decision point lands as the Houthis vow to keep hitting Saudi airports and the coalition vows a strong response.

items.title: Saudi Arabia says it downed three Houthi ballistic missiles Monday
items.summary: Saudi Arabia said it intercepted and destroyed three Houthi ballistic missiles on Monday — one over Riyadh and two over Khamis Mushait in the southwest. The Houthis claimed responsibility, saying they targeted King Khalid International Airport and a military base, and renewed warnings to airlines against flying to Saudi airports. The week's Houthi attacks have killed at least 20 people and wounded hundreds, per CNN's tally.

items.title: Saudi cuts oil shipments to European refineries after pipeline damage; UK sends advisers
items.summary: Saudi Arabia has cut some oil shipments to key European refineries after drone attacks damaged its key export pipeline, The Times reports — stoking European supply-shock fears, with diesel expected to top £2 a litre in the UK. Separately, PM Andy Burnham agreed Monday evening to RAF Voyager defensive air-to-air refuelling for Saudi jets, with a small team of British military advisers deployed to the kingdom and support beginning within days (expanding the refuelling mission first announced in September).

items.title: USS Theodore Roosevelt moves in; three US carrier groups now near region
items.summary: The USS Theodore Roosevelt is approaching the region, temporarily bringing three US aircraft carrier battle groups to the area, RANE reports — the biggest US naval concentration there in months. It lands as Trump weighs joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis and MBS lobbies him for action, and as analysts warn Riyadh could be pushed toward ground operations in Yemen.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said Monday evening the group targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh with a ballistic missile, claiming the strike was "precise," and launched a drone attack on King Khalid Air Base in Khamis Mushait, claiming a "direct hit." He renewed warnings to airlines, employees and travellers to avoid Saudi airports and airspace (except Mecca and Medina). The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed the Riyadh-bound missile; explosions were heard in the capital, residents received mobile alerts, and Civil Defense later said the danger had passed.
items.title: Saree claims new Monday-evening ballistic-missile strike on Riyadh airport; coalition says it intercepted the missile

items.summary: Saudi-led coalition airstrikes on the government complex and a citizen's home in the Khabb wa ash-Shaaf district of Al-Jawf governorate killed 9 people, including five children and a woman, and injured seven others, according to the Houthi-run health ministry. Houthi-run al-Masirah TV independently reported the same toll of nine killed and seven injured. Both sources are Houthi-affiliated; the claims could not be independently verified.
items.title: 9 killed (incl. 5 children, 1 woman), 7 injured in Saudi-led airstrikes on Al-Jawf, Yemen

items.summary: At his weekly press conference on Monday, Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei reiterated that Tehran stands ready to facilitate dialogue between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, a diplomatic overture as regional and international concern over the escalation mounts.
items.title: Iran reiterates readiness to facilitate dialogue between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis

items.summary: Yemeni military spokesperson Majid al-Nuzaili claimed government forces had carried out 1,879 attacks on Houthi military targets in recent hours, saying about 950 Houthi fighters had been "neutralized." Single-sourced claim; no independent verification reported.
items.title: Yemeni government claims 1,879 strikes on Houthi targets, ~950 fighters "neutralized"

items.event_time_ist: Monday, Oct 12 (statements; injuries from the Oct 10 strike)
items.source_name: Philippine Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) via screencap.com.ph
items.summary: The Philippine Department of Migrant Workers confirmed on Monday that 4 Filipino overseas workers were injured in the Oct 10 Houthi missile strike on King Khalid International Airport, with 3 of them in hospital intensive care in Riyadh. OWWA administrator Patricia Yvonne Caunan said at least 30 Filipinos were stranded in Riyadh (20 in DMW-OWWA sponsored hotel accommodations, 7 picked up by local relatives, 2 in-transit seafarers in airline-provided lodging); DMW secretary Hans Leo Cacdac said 94 Manila-bound and transit OFWs were diverted to Jeddah, and 37 workers stranded at Manila's NAIA terminals are receiving OWWA assistance. Cacdac confirmed there is no deployment ban on Saudi Arabia for now.
items.title: Philippines confirms 4 Filipino OFWs injured in Oct 10 Riyadh airport strike (3 in ICU); 30 stranded, 94 diverted to Jeddah

items.summary: A TV5 News graphic posted on the News5 Facebook page (dated Oct 13, using a Reuters photo of the Riyadh airport fire) claims the number of Filipinos injured in the Riyadh airport attack has risen to 7. This conflicts with the Philippine DMW's confirmed figure of 4 (3 in ICU) and could not be corroborated; treat as unverified.
items.title: TV5 graphic claims Filipino injuries in Riyadh airport attack rose to 7 — conflicts with DMW's confirmed 4

items.event_time_ist: Tuesday, Oct 13, 2026 (exact hour unverified; first reported ~5:46 PM IST)
items.summary: The Saudi-led coalition's joint forces command ordered civilians to evacuate the Yemen Oil Company's Sabah (Al-Sabahah) central fuel station in Sanaa on Tuesday, publishing a map of the site and saying to leave "for their own safety" ahead of a planned military operation (no timeline given). Spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki announced it on X. In response, Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree warned that any strike on Sanaa would draw a "harsh and painful" response in Riyadh, and the Houthis told all employees and civilians at Saudi Aramco oil facilities to evacuate and stay away, declaring them "legitimate targets." (Also reported by AP, AFP via Mint, and Gulf Business.)
items.title: Coalition orders Sanaa fuel-site evacuation ahead of operation; Houthis threaten Riyadh retaliation, warn Aramco staff to evacuate

items.summary: Coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said on X that Saudi forces shot down three drones over northern Riyadh on Tuesday, Oct 13; no attribution or damage detail given (also noted in Reuters' reporting). Same report adds: Houthi-run Al Masirah says coalition jets struck Saada province at least three times Tuesday morning after hitting northern/western areas overnight; Saree claims the Houthis downed a Saudi armed drone over Saada (unverified); and Yemen's government says Taiz clashes continued through the morning with fighter jets hitting rebel facilities nine times.
items.title: Coalition says it downed 3 drones over northern Riyadh on Tuesday; Saada hit overnight, Taiz fighting continues

items.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said it downed three Houthi ballistic missiles and two drones aimed at Riyadh and Saudi Aramco's headquarters in Dhahran on Tuesday night; a source told Reuters the HQ was struck despite the interceptions. Loud explosions rang out near the complex, the building caught fire and an evacuation order was issued, with missile fragments coming down in a nearby residential area. Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy confirmed a 'limited fire' broke out in an administrative building in Aramco's Eastern Province compound and said no injuries were reported. This is the first officially confirmed fire at an Aramco facility in this escalation.
items.title: Aramco HQ in Dhahran struck Tuesday night; limited fire in administrative building, no injuries, evacuation issued

items.summary: President Trump posted on Truth Social that the Houthis are 'behaving very badly' and have emerged again 'probably at the behest of Iran,' accusing them of hitting Saudi Arabia 'purposefully trying to drive up Oil Prices' ahead of the Nov 3 US midterms, and warned: 'I will never forget!' — hinting at possible military action after the vote. Before departing the White House he told reporters the rebels were 'behaving very badly.' He also derided Iran as a 'Failing Nation' with 'No Navy, No Airforce, the World's Worst Economy, and 301% Inflation.'
items.title: Trump blames Iran for Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, hints at military action after midterms

items.summary: Following through on the morning's evacuation warning for the Yemen Oil Company site, the Saudi-led coalition carried out new airstrikes on the Houthi-held Yemeni capital Sanaa on Tuesday, per Houthi-run Al Masirah and residents. Witnesses reported strong explosions hours after the Subaha fuel facility west of the city was struck. The Houthi oil company said its storage facilities were empty and the strike would not affect supplies; witnesses said lines of cars formed at some gas stations amid shortage fears.
items.title: Coalition carries out airstrikes on Sanaa Tuesday after fuel-site evacuation warning

items.summary: Saudi Arabia's Cabinet warned the Houthis on Tuesday that they would 'face consequences' for their repeated attacks on the kingdom, saying 'the Kingdom will not allow any threat to its security or to freedom of maritime navigation in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab Strait,' in a statement carried by state-owned Al-Ekhbariya television.
items.title: Saudi Cabinet warns Houthis will 'face consequences' for repeated attacks

items.summary: Yemen's interior ministry said Tuesday that Houthi strikes on Taiz over the past day killed six people and injured 18 amid ongoing battles; a Saudi-backed commander said rebels had reached the edges of the city and some had entered it, with the fiercest fighting over the Kahboub mountains overlooking Bab al-Mandab. UN spokesman Stephane Dujarric said Tuesday the fighting is driving large-scale displacement, cooking gas is largely unavailable and food prices have reportedly risen about 50%.
items.title: Taiz fighting intensifies: 6 killed, 18 injured in Houthi strikes over past day

items.summary: Airlines moved a number of their planes out of Riyadh on Tuesday on the advice of insurers and government officials because of the threat of additional Houthi attacks, transferring them to other airports in the country so they can keep flying passengers to their destinations, per Osprey Flight Solutions chief intelligence officer Matthew Borie. He called the move 'not abnormal' for conflict-zone situations.
items.title: Airlines ferry aircraft out of Riyadh on insurers' and officials' advice

items.summary: Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty called Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Tuesday, demanding the Houthis immediately halt attacks on Saudi Arabia — 'there is no justification for these attacks, and they cannot be accepted' — and urging diplomacy and a political solution to the Iran-US conflict to avert further escalation and instability, per the Egyptian readout.
items.title: Egypt's FM tells Iran's FM the Houthis must halt attacks on Saudi Arabia immediately
Tuesday daytime: coalition intercepts 2 ballistic missiles (Haradh, Dhahran) and 3 drones north of Riyadh
items.summary: Coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Maliki said on X that coalition forces intercepted and destroyed two Houthi ballistic missiles Tuesday — one aimed at Haradh near the Yemeni border and one toward Dhahran/eastern province — plus three Houthi drones north of Riyadh.

items.title: 4 injured in Riyadh by falling debris from Tuesday-night intercepted Houthi volley
items.summary: Saudi authorities say at least four people in the Riyadh area were injured by falling debris from the Tuesday-night Houthi volley (3 cruise missiles + 2 drones targeting Riyadh region and southern Saudi Arabia, all intercepted). A VOA Farsi graphic credited to Reuters independently reports '4 injured in Riyadh and fire in Aramco building.'

items.title: US State Dept expands airport restriction: personnel need chief-of-mission approval for ANY Saudi airport
items.summary: The US State Department expanded travel restrictions Tuesday: US government personnel in the kingdom now require special authorization from the chief of mission to use any airport in Saudi Arabia (previously Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam only). The country-level advisory was raised to Level 3 on Oct 12. Spain and Canada have also warned citizens against using the airport.

items.title: Houthi media claim civilian casualties in Tuesday coalition strikes: 2 killed/2 injured at Sanaa fuel depot; artillery deaths in Saada
items.summary: The Houthis say Tuesday's coalition strike on Al-Sabaha Central Station (their largest fuel hub in northern Yemen, ~58,000 metric tonnes; Reuters says coalition also hit sites in Hodeidah and Dhamar) killed 2 civilians and injured 2; the coalition says it warned civilians first. Al Masirah separately claims coalition artillery in Saada wounded 3 Yemenis + 2 African residents in Baqim and killed 2 civilians, wounding 2, in Shada. CNN cannot independently verify.

items.title: Saudi Arabia investigating how Houthi barrages evaded air defenses, officials tell AP
items.summary: Two regional officials speaking on condition of anonymity told the Associated Press on Tuesday that Saudi Arabia has launched an investigation into how its air defenses failed to intercept the recent barrages of Houthi missiles and drones — including the Saturday strike on King Khalid airport that killed 13.

items.title: Yemeni government claims 2,200 strikes in 24h, ~1,200 Houthi fighters killed in 'Dawn of Yemen'
items.summary: Yemeni government forces claim continued advances in the 'Dawn of Yemen' operation: 2,200 strikes against Houthi positions in the past 24 hours, about 1,200 fighters killed and 440+ military vehicles destroyed or disabled. CNN could not independently verify the figures.

items.title: Aegean cancels Riyadh flights through Oct 24; Jeddah suspended through Oct 17
items.summary: Greek carrier Aegean Airlines has canceled its Riyadh flights for the remainder of the summer 2026 season (through Oct 24) and suspended Jeddah flights through the morning arrivals of Oct 17 amid the continued King Khalid airport closure (provisional NOTAM to Oct 17 21:00 UTC).

items.source_name: SPA/Reuters via Devdiscourse; AnewZ; Al Arabiya English
items.summary: Saudi Civil Defense (via SPA) said debris from a Houthi cruise missile destroyed over Al-Kharj, south of Riyadh, fell on the capital, wounding four people (two women, a man and a child) and causing limited damage to 15 homes. The coalition also said it destroyed a drone over the Riyadh region. Al Arabiya English separately confirmed the Al-Kharj cruise-missile intercept.
items.title: Cruise missile intercepted over Al-Kharj; falling debris wounded 4, damaged 15 Riyadh homes - Civil Defense

items.summary: Yemen's Houthi-run health ministry said two people were killed in a strike on the Yemen Oil Company facility in Hodeidah, blaming Saudi Arabia for the attack. The claim came shortly after the Saudi-led coalition ordered the evacuation of the site ahead of its planned Tuesday operation.
items.title: Houthi health ministry says 2 killed in coalition strike on Hodeidah oil facility

items.summary: Reuters reports Saudi Arabia stopped issuing public warnings of imminent military attacks days before a week of deadly strikes on Riyadh's airport (four attacks, at least 18 killed per Reuters' count). The government has not said why no alerts went out; civil defence and the media office did not respond. Alerts resumed Monday Oct 12 for Riyadh and southern cities. Officials and analysts say the silence raised questions about the kingdom's vulnerability.
items.title: Reuters: Saudi warning system stayed silent before deadly airport attacks

items.summary: Saudi Arabia plans to make its flagship Future Investment Initiative conference ('Davos in the Desert') later this month a hybrid event, two people familiar with the matter told Reuters, after the deadly airport attacks prompted a rethink of travel to the kingdom. Some participants may land at airstrips outside Riyadh or in neighboring Gulf states and drive to the capital.
items.title: Saudi to make FII 'Davos in the Desert' conference hybrid after attacks - Reuters

items.source_name: GTP Headlines (corroborated by europesays/France, Travel Tomorrow, Time Out Dubai)
items.summary: British Airways plans to resume its Riyadh flights on November 3, 2026 with one daily service, as part of its staged Middle East network restoration (Dubai also Nov 3, Amman Nov 4). The plan was first announced in mid-September during the Iran-war airspace disruption, not in response to the Houthi airport strikes. Separately, GTP corroborates the FAA's Saudi advisory running until Dec 10 and EASA's conflict-zone bulletin valid until Nov 16; AirMedia24 still shows GACA with no announced reopening date beyond the provisional Oct 17 NOTAM.
items.title: British Airways to resume Riyadh flights Nov 3 (one daily); FAA advisory runs to Dec 10, EASA bulletin to Nov 16

items.source_name: WE News English (citing Saudi Press Agency)
items.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan called Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on Tuesday and condemned the Houthi attacks on Saudi territory 'in the strongest terms', per Turkey's Communications Directorate, expressing condolences for those killed and saying 'Turkiye will stand by Saudi Arabia in the coming period'. The Saudi Press Agency confirmed the call, with Erdogan affirming 'full solidarity' and support for measures safeguarding the Kingdom's security. The call lands as the Turkey-Saudi-Pakistan Makkah Joint Defence Agreement reportedly heads toward parliamentary approval in Ankara.
items.title: Erdogan condemns Houthi attacks in call with MBS, pledges Turkey's continued support

items.summary: President Trump told reporters on Tuesday that he had spoken with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman about the Houthi escalation, said the Iran-backed group was 'behaving very badly', and floated a new angle: that he may ask Turkish President Erdogan to intervene in support of Saudi Arabia. The remark adds a Turkey-mediation dimension to the US-intervention deliberation already underway since Oct 11.
items.title: Trump says Houthis 'behaving very badly', may ask Erdogan to help Saudi Arabia
Aramco HQ office tower in Dhahran hit Tuesday night: top three floors damaged, fire since extinguished
items.summary: A ballistic missile struck an office tower inside Saudi Aramco's headquarters complex in Dhahran on Tuesday night, damaging its top three floors; the building caught fire, a company source told Reuters (three people with knowledge of the matter confirmed the blaze). The Energy Ministry confirmed an 'attack' on an administrative building at the complex causing a 'limited fire', with no casualties; Bloomberg reports the fire was since extinguished. The Saudi-led coalition says fragments of a missile it intercepted and destroyed over Dhahran fell on a residential area — leaving the direct-hit vs intercept-debris accounts unresolved. The Houthis had warned oil workers to stay away from Aramco sites as 'legitimate targets.'

items.event_time_ist: Wednesday morning, Oct 14, 2026 (~10:41-10:45 AM Riyadh time announcement; launch time unverified)
items.source_name: Al Bilad Press / Kuwait News / regional breaking-news accounts (SPA-branded graphics)
items.summary: Three near-simultaneous SPA-branded Arabic breaking-news graphics posted by regional accounts (Al Bilad Press Bahrain at 10:41 AM Riyadh time, Kuwait News, and a Saudi breaking-news account) carry a coalition announcement: 'interception and destruction of a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward Riyadh.' No news outlet has yet corroborated a fresh Wednesday launch, and no casualty or debris details are reported. Caveat: the boilerplate wording matches the coalition's Monday intercept announcement, so it is possible — though the Wednesday-morning timing pattern suggests otherwise — that the graphics restate an earlier interception. Treated as a possible new event, single-sourced.
items.title: Coalition says it intercepted another Houthi ballistic missile toward Riyadh on Wednesday morning

items.event_time_ist: Wednesday morning, Oct 14 (reported 2:17 PM IST, Oct 14)
items.title: Houthis claim strikes on Aramco Dhahran, King Khalid airport and Riyadh refinery; pledge more operations
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis said on Wednesday they had targeted Saudi Aramco facilities in Dhahran, King Khalid International Airport and an Aramco refinery in Riyadh (Reuters, created 14:17 IST Oct 14), adding that their operations against airports and oil facilities would continue in the coming days. The claim follows Tuesday night's Dhahran office-tower hit (top three floors damaged, fire extinguished; Energy Ministry confirms, no casualties) and Tuesday's intercepts over Riyadh (debris wounded 4, damaged 15 homes). The Saudi side has not confirmed any Riyadh refinery damage. Regional outlets (Roya News English, ALGHAD.TV, DW Swahili) carried the same Wednesday Houthi statement as breaking news.
